title: kate-core: indent a Python line that ends in a colon
summary: python_newline copies the line indent and adds one unit when the line ends in a colon. newline_insertion stays as it is. The function carries the dead-code allowance. Linux CI runs the test.

lane.reason: The work is pure Rust in kate-core. Linux CI runs the test. The newline command still calls newline_insertion.

definitions.definition:
#[cfg_attr(not(test), allow(dead_code))]
pub fn python_newline(buf: &kate_text::TextBuffer, at: kate_text::Offset, config: &crate::DocumentConfig) -> String

data_contracts.schema_diff_summary: Add python_newline. The result starts with a newline. It copies the leading spaces and tabs on that line. When the last scalar that is not a space or a tab is a colon, append indent_unit. A width of 0 counts as 1. A line with no colon adds no extra unit. The function has cfg_attr(not(test), allow(dead_code)). newline_insertion stays as it is. The newline command still calls newline_insertion. Leave workspace.rs unchanged. The existing newline tests stay green. Leave layout.rs and notice.rs unchanged. PKT-0069 owns those files. Leave paint.rs unchanged. PKT-0071 owns that file. Leave fold.rs and view.rs unchanged. PKT-0073 owns those files. Leave command.rs and workspace.rs unchanged. PKT-0074 owns those files. Branch from the current tip of main. base_sha records that tip at planning time. If main has moved, use the new tip.

regression_tests.name: indent::tests::python_newline_adds_a_unit_after_a_colon
regression_tests.asserts: This test fails on main because python_newline does not exist. For def f(): at the end of the line, width 4 spaces, the result is a newline plus four spaces. For def f() at the end of the line, the result is only a newline.
